tool.name: Savont classify
tool.description: Classify ASVs against a reference database and build species/genus abundance tables
tool.command: mkdir -p 'staging_in' && ln -s '$asv_fasta' 'staging_in/final_asvs.fasta' && #if $feature_table ln -s '$feature_table' 'staging_in/feature-table.tsv' && #end if savont classify -i 'staging_in' -d '$db.fields.path' -o 'staging_out' -t "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" --species-threshold $thresholds.species_threshold --genus-threshold $thresholds.genus_threshold $thresholds.detailed_unclassified && cp staging_out/savont_*.log '$output_log'

param.name: asv_fasta
param.label: ASV sequences
param.help: Representative ASV sequences (``final_asvs.fasta``) as produced by **Savont ASV**.

param.name: feature_table
param.label: Feature table
param.help: Optional feature table (``feature-table.tsv`` from **Savont ASV**). It is required for runs of several pooled samples to obtain per-sample abundances; for a single sample the ASV depths are read from the sequence headers instead.

param.name: species_threshold
param.label: Species-level similarity threshold
param.help: Minimum sequence similarity (percent) to an aligning reference for an ASV to be classified at species level.

param.name: genus_threshold
param.label: Genus-level similarity threshold
param.help: Minimum sequence similarity (percent) to an aligning reference for an ASV to be classified at genus level.

param.name: detailed_unclassified
param.label: Report detailed unclassified ASVs
param.help: Also classify ASVs that fall below the species-level threshold, reporting the best matching reference.

tool.help:
**Savont classify** aligns the representative ASV sequences produced by **Savont ASV** against a Savont reference database (for example the EMU 16S rRNA database) and assigns a taxonomy to every ASV.
An ASV is classified at *species* level when its similarity to the best aligning reference sequence reaches the species-level threshold (99% by default) and at *genus* level when it reaches the genus-level threshold (94.5% by default). Ambiguous cases, in which several references match similarly, are resolved with an EM algorithm that distributes the ASV abundance over the candidate taxa.
Inputs ------
* **ASV sequences**: the ``final_asvs.fasta`` output of **Savont ASV**. * **Feature table** *(optional)*: the ``feature-table.tsv`` output of **Savont ASV**. It is the authoritative source of the per-sample ASV abundances and must be supplied for runs that pooled several samples. * **Savont reference database**: a database installed with the *Savont reference databases* data manager.
Outputs -------
* **Species abundance table**: relative abundance per taxonomic level, one row per species. * **Genus abundance table**: the same, one row per genus. * **ASV mappings**: the taxonomic assignment of every ASV with the alignment statistics used to make the assignment.
**classify** works best for species/strain-level assignment. If your microbiome is not well captured by the chosen reference database, consider **Savont SINTAX**, which classifies at genus level with k-mer bootstrapping.
